name: 415. xAI video, text to speech and speech to text meet the contract (xai media contract)
description: Pins TXE-6429 (contract C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C9) for the xai provider on POST /v1/videos, GET /v1/videos/{id}, GET /v1/videos/{id}/content, POST /v1/videos/{id}/cancel, POST /v1/audio/speech and POST /v1/audio/transcriptions. Local fixture regression, no live provider calls: start tests/e2e/api/runners/provider-error-fixture.mjs, start an isolated gateway on tests/e2e/api/provider_config/provider-error-fixture.config.json and run with providerErrorFixture=1; every case is skipped otherwise. The xai provider's base is the fixture's /pp/xai, so every vendor call is a row of GET /__wire. Before the change xai answered every one of these operations with an unsupported-operation error. Rows 2 and 3: a video create converts the unified fields to xAI's own (seconds to duration, input_reference to image.url, last_frame, reference_images, output_storage_uri to output.upload_url) and merges the extra fields unchanged. Rows 4 to 8: callback_url, client_reference_id, expires_after_seconds, a size xAI cannot produce and a fractional seconds are 400 caller_unsupported_parameter. Row 9: cancel is 400 provider_cancel_unsupported. Row 10: a usage-policy refusal keeps xAI's 403 and body and is caller_content_filtered. Rows 11 to 13: the task object carries provider_status, usage{output_tokens, output_seconds, vendor_cost in usd_ticks} and a url artifact; a moderated task is failed with content_filter. Row 14 creates on an upstream that reads the request and drops the connection; it follows three queries, which leave a keep-alive connection in the provider's shared pool, the one a resend would come from. Row 15 reads the wire: the dropped create arrived exactly once (xAI cannot find a task again, so a second copy would be a second billed task) and no refused request arrived at all. Rows 16 to 20: speech returns xAI's audio bytes, decodes the with_timestamps envelope and reports its duration in x-bifrost-usage, refuses instructions and a codec xAI does not produce, and sends /v1/tts its own fields. Rows 21 to 24: a transcription returns usage{type: duration, seconds} and words, takes a url in place of the file, refuses response_format, and writes file as the last form field with repeated fields once per value. Rows 25 to 28: the download. The gateway's media fetcher refuses loopback, so the provider xai_media_proxy (the xAI base, with this fixture as its HTTP forward proxy) is given a link under 203.0.113.10 (TEST-NET-3, never routed), which the fixture answers as the proxy. The video comes back as video/mp4, a thumbnail variant is 400 caller_unsupported_parameter, a pending task is a 400, and the wire shows one task query and one fetch of the link with no Authorization header.
